verdict.line: You lose if you walk into Cannon-stance pokes before level 6; you win if you survive to Hextech Ultimatum and let Trinity Force scaling take over.

brief.thesis: Jayce's stance swap is the whole lane: in Cannon stance his Shock Blast pokes you from 600 range and you have nothing to answer it with until level 6. Once Camille hits R, Hextech Ultimatum gives her a 475-range dash onto Jayce regardless of walls, which is the first reliable gap-close she's had all lane. The 54.1% win rate over 2,517 games reflects exactly that pattern — she isn't winning the poke war, she's winning the game that starts after it.

theirWindow.when: Jayce sits in Cannon stance at range
theirWindow.what: He's fishing with Shock Blast (16/14/12/10/8s cooldown) and can detonate it on you from 600 range before you're close enough to answer. Don't walk up to farm through this — hold position and let minions soak it, or trade back immediately with W (Tactical Sweep) once he fires since its outer half slows and heals you off the damage you just ate.

yourWindow.when: His Q and E are both down, or you have R
yourWindow.what: With Shock Blast/To the Skies! and Thundering Blow both on cooldown Jayce has no way to slow, knock back, or gap-close away from you — walk him down and use E (Hookshot) off any nearby wall for the knockup into Q into W. From level 6 onward you don't even need the wall: R (Hextech Ultimatum) dashes you onto him from 475 range and anchors him in place for the fight.

powerCurve.note: Trade pokes; W's outer cone heals through his autos
Full Cannon poke online, you have no gap-close
R lands the dash his kit can't escape

start.why: Run at 55.1% over 1,886 games and picked 66.5% of the time in this matchup — the passive block and sustain directly offset Jayce's poke-based autos and Shock Blast chip damage before you have an answer for it.

boots.why: 81.2% pick rate at 54.5% win rate; Jayce's entire kit hits as physical damage (autos, Shock Blast, To the Skies!), so the flat auto-attack reduction matters more here than Mercury's Treads' tenacity.

core.why: First item in the 60.4%-winrate, 48.8%-pick path — the move speed and bonus damage proc are what let you actually close the gap once R or a wall is available.
Second item in every top core path listed; the sustain and wave clear let you shove and threaten all-ins instead of just surviving poke.
Most popular third item (48.8% of this path) — damage mitigation against his burst combo while you close distance, which is the single hardest part of this lane.

situational.when: jayce or his team is stacking burst and you need to survive his all-in instead of just outlasting poke
you're ahead by level 10 and want the cooldown refund to chain R-Q-W engages faster
lane is shoving hard and you need the early wave clear/sustain before finishing Hydra

runes.keystoneWhy: Bonus max health and a free proc every few seconds directly answers a lane defined by chip damage from range — you need the health pool and sustain more than burst keystone damage this early.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport runs 54.2% over a 24.8% pick rate — Teleport lets you play the lane patiently (per OP.GG's own read that Camille wins if she doesn't die early) and still reset to lane or impact sidelines once you've stabilized past level 6.

playing.title: Track his stance, not his HP
playing.detail: Cannon stance means he's a poke threat at 600 range; Hammer stance means his E (Thundering Blow) can knock you back on contact. Your positioning should change the instant he swaps.

playing.title: Use W proactively, not reactively
playing.detail: Tactical Sweep's outer half slows and heals you off whatever damage lands — throw it into his poke exchanges even if you don't expect to land the inner hit, since the delayed cone still trades back health.

playing.title: Don't engage without a wall or R
playing.detail: Before level 6, only commit with E (Hookshot) when a wall is in range for the knockup. Walking up without it just hands Jayce a free Thundering Blow knockback or Shock Blast.

playing.title: Save Flash for his E knockback, not his poke
playing.detail: Thundering Blow's knockback (20/18/16/14/12s cooldown) is his main tool to peel you off once you've closed the gap — don't burn Flash dodging pre-6 pokes you can just walk around.

playing.title: All-in the moment R is up
playing.detail: Hextech Ultimatum anchors him in place and gives bonus magic damage on your autos for the fight — this is your first game-even engage tool, so look for it on cooldown from level 6 onward rather than waiting for a perfect read.

playing.title: Don't force kills before 6
playing.detail: The matchup is even on solo kills and lane advantage — trading evenly and hitting level 6 even is a win. You don't need to win levels 1-5, you need to survive them.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, boots, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/pick-rate figures are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch (16.19.1); the stance-tracking, cooldown-window, and engage-timing analysis is my own read on why those numbers come out this way.

stats.opponentTip: Be careful of Jayce’s ranged pokes! Use [W] constantly to ease managing health in lane! Camille has the upper hand in the late game if she did not die early on.
